requirement:
The harness MUST expose an `outline` tool with this interface:

```text
outline({ file: String }) -> Array<OutlineEntry>

OutlineEntry {
    item: String,
    kind: String,
    name: String?,
    children: Array<OutlineEntry>,
}
```

The tool MUST return the outline of a permitted file in a supported language
under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, with each node's selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, its kind, and its name when it
is named, nested by outline ancestry and in source order. Results MUST contain
no source text or line numbers and MUST NOT become evidence inputs; the model reads
the nodes it relies on with the `habeas` tool. For a file using the plain-text
profile, the outline lists its `line` nodes. Explicitly requesting an excluded
file MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
rationale:
The tests marked for `requirements.authoring.outline_tool` cover each obligation the text states. One exclusion mode is covered only by a test that lacks the marker, which I treat as a minor marking gap and not an adequacy gap.

**Interface**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_is_advertised_with_a_required_file_argument]` asserts the exact parameter schema. It requires a string `file`, makes it required, and sets `additionalProperties` to false. It also checks the description's key phrases: item selector, kind, name, no line numbers, no source text, and reading nodes with habeas.
- `fn[outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs]` checks malformed arguments. It tries `{}`, a non-string `file`, an extra argument and a missing file. Each case must return an error that names the problem.

**Outline content**
- The same test asserts the exact JSON for a Rust file. Entries have `item`, `kind`, `name` and `children`. `struct[Thing]` comes before `impl[Thing]`, and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]` is nested under it. This covers selectors, kinds, names, nesting and source order.
- It also covers a trait impl, `impl[Thing/Trait]`. The exact-equality assertion means an extra line-number field would fail it.
- The doc comment `/// Docs.` must not appear anywhere in the result, so source text is excluded.
- A plain-text file with a blank line yields exactly two entries. Each has kind `line`, a null name, an item starting with `line@`, and no `line_start` field. That covers the plain-text profile and the skipping of blank lines.

**Not evidence inputs**
- `assert!(outline.inputs.is_empty())` covers this for the Rust outline. `unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors` asserts that no inputs are recorded after denied outline requests.

**Excluded file handled as a denial under `requirements.authoring.read_denial`**
- With `notes.txt` disallowed in `habeas.toml`, the outline request must fail with `PermissionDenied`. The error message must name `notes.txt` and contain "disallowed", so it gives the path and the reason.
- `unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors` checks that an outline request for a path outside the project is a recoverable error. Its second half checks that a matching disallow rule still gives `PermissionDenied`.
- Other kinds of exclusion are covered by tests that lack an `outline_tool` marker. These are an untracked file, in `git_tools_allow_staged_and_dirty_sources_but_hide_untracked_files`, and a symlink leaving the project. The untracked test asserts `PermissionDenied` and a "git add" hint. The marked tests already exercise the shared denial path through the `outline` tool, so I count these unmarked ones only as a marking gap, not an adequacy gap.

**Out of scope**
- Per-language outline profiles for languages other than Rust and plain text belong to `requirements.references.outlines`. Selector syntax belongs to `outline_selectors`. Neither needs separate tests here.
- The marked `OutlineCache` tests in `src/inputs.rs` only support the implementation. They are not needed for adequacy.

No obligation of the text is left unasserted, and none of the plausible violations is accepted by the tests. A violation would be returning source text or line numbers, recording inputs, nesting wrongly, or treating a disallowed file as a plain read failure.

text: :::{req} outline_tool
The harness MUST expose an `outline` tool with this interface:
```text
outline({ file: String }) -> Array<OutlineEntry>
OutlineEntry {
item: String,
kind: String,
name: String?,
children: Array<OutlineEntry>,
The tool MUST return the outline of a permitted file in a supported language
under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines`, with each node's selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`, its kind, and its name when it
is named, nested by outline ancestry and in source order. Results MUST contain
no source text or line numbers and MUST NOT become evidence inputs; the model reads
the nodes it relies on with the `habeas` tool. For a file using the plain-text
profile, the outline lists its `line` nodes. Explicitly requesting an excluded
file MUST be handled as a denial under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. When validating outline evidence inputs, Habeas MUST report
the line of the first syntax error in a recovered outline. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
:::{req} read_denial
When source-access policy denies a path that a model tool call names
explicitly, the harness MUST return a tool error naming the path and the reason
it cannot be read, add no evidence input, and continue the assessment.
Discovery and search MUST leave denied candidates out of their entries,
reporting untracked ones under {cite}`requirements.authoring.not_listed`. Malformed tool
arguments and ordinary read failures MUST also return explanatory tool errors.
